transitions.effects: Launch process; start stdout queue and stderr reader threads.
transitions.failure_retry: Streams/message lists are retained in memory; per-read timeout is not a total session deadline or global output cap.

transitions.guard: Matching request id, object result and correct codexHome
transitions.effects: Send initialized notification, then skills/list with forceReload.
transitions.failure_retry: Error response, malformed JSON, EOF or missing response raises a protocol failure.

transitions.guard: Exactly one namespaced selected skill, absolute installed path and matching bytes
transitions.effects: Bind selected skill and installed root.
transitions.failure_retry: Missing, duplicate or relative skill selection cannot advance as successful proof.

transitions.guard: Thread id and actual effective readOnly sandbox with networkAccess=false
transitions.effects: Request never approval and ephemeral thread; retain observed effective policies.
transitions.failure_retry: Requested policy does not replace the returned effective policy.

transitions.guard: Explicit skill input plus constrained read instructions
transitions.effects: Collect notification stream until turn/completed; record completed command events.
transitions.failure_retry: Every _next wait is bounded20seconds; continuous notifications can extend the overall operation.

transitions.guard: Completed status and valid final agent JSON plus successful exact command evidence
transitions.effects: Inject host-observed requested/effective policy into observation and validate through common receipt builder.
transitions.failure_retry: Non-completed status or protocol failure yields errors; the last textual claim is not sufficient.

transitions.guard: Regardless of probe success
transitions.effects: Close stdin, wait2seconds, terminate then kill on successive timeouts, join reader threads and close streams.
transitions.failure_retry: This is bounded staged shutdown of the direct process; it is not a claim of arbitrary descendant-process containment.

machines.name: Candidate package snapshot and resource closure
machines.state_storage: Ephemeral collector process, isolated temporary profile, exact candidate bytes, explicitly supplied durable receipts
machines.state_notation: Analytical phases over actual branches, subprocesses and evidence; literal verdicts and durable evidence states are identified in the rows.

transitions.guard: Regular non-symlink/reparse root and supported shape
transitions.effects: Reject unsafe entries, encrypted ZIP members, invalid modes, path escapes, normalized collisions and expansion limits.
transitions.failure_retry: Validation does not install or execute candidate bytes.

transitions.guard: Same device/inode as enumerated regular file; size within declared bounds
transitions.effects: Read bounded bytes and reject changes beyond declared size; verify permitted promoted large binaries against receipt hashes.
transitions.failure_retry: Large-file exception is narrow and receipt-bound, not a general bypass of candidate bounds.

transitions.guard: Any selected helper/consumer marker activates the whole required local set
transitions.effects: Require named helper/consumer resources and expected contract entry markers.
transitions.failure_retry: Marker presence is static packaging evidence, not proof that runtime delivery succeeds.

transitions.guard: UTF8 and supported link grammar; contained resolvable local Markdown links or named templates
transitions.effects: Record selected file hashes and relative-read edges in deterministic order.
transitions.failure_retry: Remote links are not fetched; approved symbolic template destinations are not mistaken for concrete existing files.

transitions.guard: ca-codex identity, valid version, names match paths, exact approved hook manifest digest and present targets
transitions.effects: Produce package/resource digests and selected paths.
transitions.failure_retry: An approved hook inventory digest proves the static contract only, not host hook invocation.

transitions.guard: Complete inert validation result
transitions.effects: Print structured or human result.
transitions.failure_retry: No live authenticated turn or publication is implied by this lane.

machines.name: Constrained Markdown link parser context
machines.state_storage: Ephemeral collector process, isolated temporary profile, exact candidate bytes, explicitly supplied durable receipts
machines.state_notation: Analytical phases over actual branches, subprocesses and evidence; literal verdicts and durable evidence states are identified in the rows.

transitions.event: Open fenced/quoted/list/indented code or HTML literal
transitions.guard: Recognized grammar and current fence/indent state
transitions.effects: Blank literal characters while preserving offsets/newlines; retain specially recognized symbolic destination segments.
transitions.failure_retry: A filename match inside code or an HTML literal is not automatically a resource edge.

transitions.guard: Matching fence character/length, quote/list continuation rules
transitions.effects: Resume link interpretation outside literal regions.
transitions.failure_retry: Unmatched literal delimiters retain their actual parser behavior; not a general CommonMark library guarantee.

transitions.guard: Matched delimiter or recognized literal form
transitions.effects: Ignore code spans, escaped references and image-like regions for resource links.
transitions.failure_retry: An unmatched code span is left visible by this scanner.

transitions.guard: Balanced labels, parentheses depth<=32 and supported optional title
transitions.effects: Unescape supported punctuation and return target with occupied span.
transitions.failure_retry: Malformed/unsupported/unterminated destination or title raises explicit ValueError.

transitions.guard: Unique normalized label; existing definition for full/collapsed reference
transitions.effects: Resolve supported full/collapsed/defined shortcut references outside occupied spans.
transitions.failure_retry: Duplicate or unresolved reference-style definitions fail instead of guessing a target.

transitions.guard: Opening/closing delimiter, unique allowed key grammar and required nonempty fields
transitions.effects: Decode supported quoted scalar values and verify name/path relation in package owner.
transitions.failure_retry: Multiline/unsupported front matter is rejected by this deliberately constrained parser, not silently interpreted as YAML.

findings.title: Conflict command prescribes a broader stop than the assistive engine contract
findings.detail: The conflict command says all work stops when governing rules conflict. Current sprint/context guidance and ADR0043 describe refusal scoped to dependent work. These cannot both be a universal rule. Source does not implement a single dependency-aware conflict controller.
findings.recommendation: Choose and document the stop scope explicitly. Recommend stop affected authority/data dependencies, preserve independent read-only work, and keep genuine global host/user stops global. This is a policy decision, not a silent prose cleanup.

findings.title: Debug handoff treats a correctable packet error as a terminal one-shot boundary
findings.detail: The workflow forbids repairing and resubmitting any rejected packet. The validator is stateless and distinguishes malformed/invalid packets from internal I/O errors; it records no consumed one-shot capability. The prose therefore imposes an extra recovery policy beyond implementation.
findings.recommendation: Separate invalid input, denied authority, stale binding and internal failure. Permit an explicitly corrected new input attempt where authority remains valid; retain the refusal for an unchanged denied request. Requires approved workflow-policy change.

findings.title: Maintenance severity and reviewer disposition conflict
findings.detail: The dependency reviewer can report HIGH maintenance risk while saying not to block on maintenance alone. The included reviewer contract says every HIGH is blocking and additions never replace that rule. This makes a correct verdict ambiguous for the reviewing agent and user.
findings.recommendation: Represent severity and disposition separately; document the explicit maintenance-only disposition exception or revise its severity. Generate the common verdict contract from the selected policy.

findings.title: Terminal finding harvest has no implemented recovery for interruption before the terminal step
findings.detail: Several workflows harvest qualifying findings at completion. The knowledge helper and session/standup paths do not implement a durable pending-harvest backstop. An interrupted run can therefore leave eligible findings only in conversation; the source does not prove every such finding is lost.
findings.recommendation: Keep harvest opportunistic. If durable recovery is desired, record bounded pending candidates at discovery and settle/deduplicate on completion/resume. Register any new output with all native readers; do not introduce a new universal completion gate.

findings.title: SessionStart persona documentation contradicts the prompt-submit owner
findings.detail: Init/porting language attributes persona injection to SessionStart. The implemented SessionStart path and ADR0030 place full composed persona delivery in UserPromptSubmit; a mode revisitation bug is documented separately in the hooks findings.
findings.recommendation: Make prompt-submit the documented delivery owner and distinguish session setup, selected mode, committed mode and delivered persona.

findings.title: Sensitive-lines-only override wording understates the implemented candidate binding
findings.detail: The override surface describes an invalidation scope around sensitive lines. The security pass and binding helper retain full candidate/worktree/sensitive digests and hash the complete staged UTF8 diff. A user cannot reliably predict grant reuse from the narrower wording.
findings.recommendation: Document the exact binding tuple and invalidation event. Preserve current security semantics while deriving override help from the same binding definition.

findings.title: Watch confuses absence of agent polling with absence of CLI polling
findings.detail: The watch command describes gh pr checks --watch as server-side blocking with no polling interval. The official gh command documents --interval with default10seconds. Waiting in one detached CLI invocation avoids model-driven polling, but the underlying CLI still refreshes periodically.
findings.recommendation: Say one detached gh watch process with no repeated agent calls; preserve its timeout/cancel behavior. Correct the no-polling claim.

findings.title: Command catalog and reviewer index drift from their owner bodies
findings.detail: COMMANDS.md calls Tribunal eleven-lens while the current owner/reference set contains thirteen. Its release signature uses --dry-run and SemVer-only language where the current owner uses --dryrun and supports numeric sequence targets. The agent index also presents coverage behavior more strongly than the coverage reviewer body does.
findings.recommendation: Generate signatures, lens count and index descriptions from explicit owner metadata; do not change actual command spelling or verdict rules just to match stale summaries.

findings.title: Compatibility-removal metadata encodes a different policy than the public owner
findings.detail: command-routes.json removalRequires is minor-release-with-changelog-notice. build-surface.py enforces that literal vocabulary. The command compatibility policy describes a major/1.0 floor plus a separate approved removal decision and fresh evidence. The release-state observer does not enforce removalRequires. This is a dormant metadata/policy conflict, not proof of an unauthorized live alias removal.
findings.recommendation: Choose the approved retirement rule, give it one owner and generate both policy prose and accepted registry values. Preserve existing aliases until the separately approved removal conditions are met.

coverage.root_workflow_reads: See root-read-files.json; behavioral phase names are analytical, not undocumented enum claims.
